payload.claim: `_REGULAR_MODES = ("100644", "100755")` restates, under the exact name of `saffron/repos/mirror.py`'s own `_REGULAR_MODES`, a constant the repository already defines there. `docs/backlog/b-385eba-the-regular-file-modes-are-spelled-three-times.md` already tracks this very tuple being spelled in three modules and says 'Done looks like: One public constant, imported by all three modules.' The spec's `touches` list (frontmatter) excludes `saffron/repos/mirror.py`, so this task could not import the existing constant, but reusing its private name for a locally-defined, differently-typed (`tuple` here, `set` in `mirror.py`) value adds a fourth occurrence of the same fact under a name that now collides across two unrelated modules, worsening rather than narrowing the tracked debt. Per the 'one source' rule ('a type, a constant or a helper the repository already defines' should be imported rather than restated), this is a call for the operator: whether to fold this new occurrence into b-385eba now, or rename the local constant so it stops sharing `mirror.py`'s private name.
